newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 1996/97 cap injections, privatisation funds.
newsitem.headline: French 1996/97 cap injections, privatisation funds.

text.p: The French finance ministry said on Friday capital injections into state firms so far announced for 1997 came to 32.1 billion and these would be met by existing and projected privatisation receipts of more than 37 billion francs.

The information was contained in a statement issued the day after the government said it would inject 11 billion francs into state-controlled insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN) this year as part of a 20-billion-franc rescue package.
It said it had "more than 10 billion francs" in unspent 1996 privatisation receipts and the 1997 budget estimated revenues of 27 billion francs from state sell-offs this year.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis stressed on Thursday that the GAN rescue would not impinge on the national budget in 1997, the year for measuring whether public deficits are limited to three percent of GDP in line with the Maastricht treaty criteria for joining european economic and monetary union in 1999.
Following are figures supplied by the ministry for capital injections/transactions in 1996, in billions of francs.
No figure is given for Credit Lyonnais or Thomson and the money for GIAT came from budget credit transfers rather than privatisation receipts, the statement said.
Credit Lyonnais and Thomson no figure given

NOTE: The government plans to sell a stake in France Telecom by public offer in May and a France Telecom spokesman said on February 19 the flotation would be for "at least 25 billion francs."

Jean Arthuis said on February 27 when he announced the GAN bail-out that he planned to sell off the GAN banking subsidiary Credit Industriel et Commercial and GAN Assurances "during the course of 1997."

After abandoning plans to sell off the defence and consumer electronics group Thomson SA, the government has decided to go ahead with the privatisation by trade sale of the Thomson-CSF defence electronics arm and recapitalise the Thomson Multimedia (TMM) consumer electronics arm pending a decision on what to do with TMM.
Ministry sources said on February 20 the aim is to sell off Thomson-CSF "during the summer."
The now-defunct plan to privatise Thomson SA involved a sale for one symbolic franc.
